summary: The feature 'capital-gain' is the most important predictor of income, with a mean importance score of 0.1507 across 3x5-fold cross-validation. This finding is stable across multiple evaluation methods and consistent in rankings.
methodological_choices: Random Forest classifier (100 trees, max_depth=20) trained on preprocessed data. Missing values filled with median (numerical) or mode (categorical). All features label-encoded. Importance measured using built-in feature_importances_ from tree-based model. Validation: 3 repeats × 5-fold stratified cross-validation with different random seeds, plus hold-out test set (80/20 split).
verification_method: 3 different approaches: (1) Train on full data, (2) 3 repeats of 5-fold stratified cross-validation with different seeds, (3) Hold-out test set (80/20 split). All three methods ranked the same feature as most important.
verification_result: Finding is STABLE. Across all three validation methods, 'capital-gain' consistently ranks as the top feature. CV mean ± std: 0.1507 ± 0.0013. It appears in the top-3 features in all 15 CV folds.
